name: The Forth Bridge
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: This red cantilever railway bridge crosses the Firth of Forth in eastern Scotland, about 14 km west of Edinburgh, linking South Queensferry and North Queensferry. When it opened in 1890 it had the longest spans in the world, and trains still rumble across its 2.5 km length today. Its giant, unadorned steel framework makes it one of Scotland's best-loved landmarks.
